disease_label_per_paper: Colonic involvement in disseminated histoplasmosis of an immunocompetent adult
presentation_summary: 33-year-old immunocompetent man was admitted with more than three months of intermittent moderate fever, night sweats, anorexia, and 15 kg weight loss.
He had no obvious cough or expectoration, no known immunodeficiency, no travel to Kala-azar or histoplasmosis-endemic areas, but reported occasional damp working environment exposure.
Admission vitals showed temperature 37.7 C, heart rate 94/min, respiratory rate 25/min, and blood pressure 96/64 mmHg.
Admission labs showed pancytopenia with hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, WBC 3.2 x10^9/L, platelets 92 x10^9/L, ESR 61 mm/hr, and alkaline phosphatase 277 IU/L; HIV tests were repeatedly negative.
Chest CT was normal, abdominal CT/ultrasound showed hepatosplenomegaly, colonoscopy showed diffuse aphthoid colonic ulcers, and bone marrow plus colon specimens confirmed Histoplasma.

imaging.source_text_value: colonoscopy showed strictures, edematous mucosa and diffuse aphthoid ulcers measuring 0.5-1.0 cm in diameter scattered throughout the mucous membrane of the colon

lab_trajectories.source_text_value: A blood test before the patient was discharged showed hemoglobin levels of 12.3 g/dL

confirmatory_findings.finding: Bone marrow aspirate showed organisms highly suggestive of Histoplasma capsulatum
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Hematoxylin and eosin stained bone marrow aspirate demonstrated oval or round organisms ... highly suggestive of Histoplasmosis capsulatum

confirmatory_findings.finding: Bone marrow biopsy PAS and GMS stains were positive and compatible with histoplasmosis
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Sections of bone marrow biopsy stained with PAS ... and GMS ... were both positive, which was compatible with a diagnosis of histoplasmosis

confirmatory_findings.finding: Colon biopsy showed yeast-like structures with PAS and GMS positivity consistent with histoplasmosis
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Biopsy specimens of the colon identified numerous yeast-like structures ... staining positive for PAS stain, and GMS stain ... consistent with histoplasmosis

actual_treatment: intravenous amphotericin B deoxycholate started at 1 mg/day and increased to 50 mg once daily
temperature returned to normal and appetite improved one week after treatment
amphotericin B deoxycholate continued for two months with a total dose of 2000 mg
shifted to oral itraconazole 200 mg twice daily before discharge

outcome.source_text_value: One week after treatment, the patient's temperature returned to normal levels, and his appetite improved ... follow-up CT scan showed the spleen had returned to a normal size ... Enteroscopy performed 2 months after treatment showed that the ulcers and congestion of mucosa were recovering

quality_warnings: Bone marrow and colon pathology are confirmatory_findings only; ordinary observations use fever, vitals, cytopenias, ESR/ALP, hepatosplenomegaly, and colonic ulcer morphology.
Weight-loss rate uses 12 weeks as a conservative denominator for 'more than 3 months'; true rate may be lower if the duration was substantially longer.
CD4 240 was preserved as a measured host-context value, but the paper argues it was transient and secondary to systemic infection rather than the cause.
